note: Registers the Security+ pathway so it appears beside the other pathways. Its course text lives in the secplus-*.json files and loads on demand, so it is not copied into your saved data.

pathway.title: Security+ for Product Designers — CompTIA SY0-801
pathway.summary: One 16-week pathway with two outcomes: readiness for Security+ V8 and the ability to apply security knowledge as a Senior Product Designer. Every official objective, labs and two timed mock exams, with design exercises inside the lessons where they truly apply. Independent of CompTIA.
pathway.forWho: Product designers preparing for Security+ SY0-801, including those with no IT background, with about 9 to 13 hours in most weeks. Questions are AI-written, so read the policy note on the pathway's first page.

lessons.title: Start here: how Security+ for Product Designers works
lessons.inOneSentence: This pathway has its own pages for lessons, labs, design exercises, knowledge checks, mock exams and two separate progress measures.
lessons.youCanNow: Open the pathway, understand how it tracks technical mastery and design competency separately, and decide whether its AI-written material suits you.
lessons.whyItMattersToADesigner: Each security concept is connected directly to how it appears in products and how you would design for it, so exam preparation and professional practice build on each other.
keyIdeas: The first four weeks are foundations and are not exam domains.
Each lesson has six parts: learn the concept, technical deep dive, see it in real products, apply it as a Product Designer, test your understanding, then review.
Security+ mastery and design competency are measured separately. Neither can raise the other.
The practice questions are AI-written and are not authorized by CompTIA. Read CompTIA's policy on the pathway's first page before relying on them.

words.meaning: The exam code for CompTIA Security+ version 8.

steps.text: Open the pathway from Learn → Pathways and read its first page, including the policy note.
Open the progress dashboard to see how the two measures work.

lessons.skipOrSkim: Nothing to skip. This is a short orientation.
checkYourself: Why does finishing all 16 weeks not mean that you are ready for the exam?
Why doesn't passing a question about OAuth show that you can design an OAuth experience?
lookFor: Readiness in this pathway depends on demonstrated results: objective status, mock exam scores and performance-based practice.
Knowing a concept and designing for it are different skills, which is why they are assessed separately.
